dedupe_keys.name: new york city optimal dynamic climate adaptation pathways by real options and extreme value theory

description: This study sets out a method for choosing optimal adaptation pathways, the order and timing of investments in a portfolio of climate adaptation projects, and applies it to coastal flood and storm surge protection for New York City. Chi Truong, Matteo Malavasi, Han Li, Stefan Trück and Pavel Shevchenko of Macquarie University, UNSW Sydney and the University of Melbourne posted it on arXiv in February 2024. Extreme sea levels at the Battery gauge in lower Manhattan, from 1920 to 2019, are modelled with the block maxima approach of extreme value theory, and a real options framework adds sea level rise uncertainty and growth in exposed asset values. Candidate projects include wet-proofing buildings, for example 2 feet of wet-proofing at US$246 million, other flood-proofing measures, and hard defences such as a barrier and dikes, and sensitivity analysis tests the discount rate and sea level rise assumptions. Coverage is New York City. Format and access: open preprint using public University of Hawaii Sea Level Center data; no code release was seen. Licence: arXiv licence not read; free to read. Caveats: damage functions and project costs come from earlier studies. It supports climate adaptation and optimisation of investment timing for coastal defences. Related catalogue records are the Thames Estuary 2100 adaptive plan and the PSMSL tide gauge data bank on the register branch.
